whatItIs.heading: What is water damage restoration?
whatItIs.body: Water damage restoration is the full-cycle process of returning a home or building to its pre-loss condition after a water intrusion event. It starts the moment water enters the structure and ends when walls, floors, and fixtures are rebuilt and dry. The process covers emergency water removal to stop ongoing damage, extraction of standing water, structural drying with industrial air movers and dehumidifiers, moisture mapping to confirm dryness inside wall cavities and subfloors, contamination remediation when gray or black water is involved, and the final reconstruction phase—drywall, flooring, cabinetry, paint. Water damage restoration is not the same as a simple cleanup or a plumber fixing the source; it addresses the structural and biological consequences left behind.

process.heading: How Gallagher handles water damage restoration

steps.title: Emergency response and assessment
steps.body: A real person answers at any hour. Gallagher Restoration Co. targets on-site arrival within 60 minutes across the five-county area. The crew identifies the water source, documents affected areas with thermal imaging, and classifies contamination category before touching anything.

steps.title: Extraction and emergency mitigation
steps.body: Professional-grade truck-mounted and portable extractors remove standing water immediately. Safety cutoffs are engaged on electrical circuits in saturated zones. Contaminated materials—soaked carpet, pad, damaged drywall—that cannot be dried in place are removed to prevent mold colonization.

steps.title: Structural drying and moisture mapping
steps.body: Industrial air movers and commercial dehumidifiers run continuously, typically three to five days. Technicians take daily moisture readings at wall cavities, subfloor, and structural members using calibrated meters. Drying is documented in writing for your insurance claim.

steps.title: Reconstruction and final handoff
steps.body: The same Gallagher crew transitions directly into rebuild—replacing drywall, flooring, cabinetry, and paint. No subcontractor handoff, no scheduling gap. The job closes with a final moisture clearance reading and a walkthrough with the homeowner.

signs.heading: Signs you need water damage restoration now
signs.intro: Visible water is the obvious trigger, but secondary signs often mean damage has already spread beyond what you can see.

items.title: Standing or pooling water indoors
items.body: Any standing water inside the structure requires immediate extraction. Every hour it sits, water migrates further into flooring, wall framing, and insulation.

items.title: Soft, buckling, or discolored flooring
items.body: Hardwood that cups, tile grout that darkens, or laminate that swells all indicate moisture has reached the subfloor. Waiting accelerates delamination and structural decay.

items.title: Water stains or bubbling paint on ceilings and walls
items.body: Discoloration on drywall signals active or recent moisture intrusion. Bubbling or peeling paint means water is already behind the surface and drying has begun—in the wrong direction.

items.title: Musty odor without visible mold
items.body: A persistent earthy or sour smell typically means mold is colonizing inside wall cavities or below flooring—areas that look dry at the surface but test wet with a moisture meter.

items.title: Sudden spike in water or utility bills
items.body: An unexplained jump in water usage often points to a slab leak or hidden pipe burst. By the time the bill arrives, the moisture has had weeks to migrate.

pricing.heading: Water damage restoration pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Every job starts with a free on-site assessment; there is no charge to show up, diagnose, and document. Most water damage restoration projects in Southern California fall in the $500–$15,000 range. The low end covers a small clean-water spill contained to a single room with no structural saturation. The upper end reflects multi-room events involving Category 2 or Category 3 water—gray or black water contamination—where affected materials must be removed, the structure must be sanitized, and reconstruction spans multiple rooms. Scope, contamination category, square footage, and how quickly mitigation began all drive the final number. Gallagher Restoration Co. works directly with your insurance carrier and builds the documentation package the adjuster needs from day one.

faqs.q: How long does water damage restoration take?
faqs.a: Structural drying alone typically takes three to five days. The full restoration timeline—extraction through reconstruction—runs one to three weeks for most residential jobs, depending on scope, contamination category, and how quickly materials dry. Larger or multi-room events with mold involvement take longer.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover water damage restoration in California?
faqs.a: Most standard homeowners policies in California cover sudden and accidental water damage—burst pipes, appliance failures, roof leaks from a storm. Gradual leaks and flood damage from rising groundwater are typically excluded. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents the cause and scope from day one and coordinates directly with your adjuster.

faqs.q: Can I stay in my home during water damage restoration?
faqs.a: It depends on the extent of damage and the contamination category. Clean-water events in a single room often allow normal occupancy while drying equipment runs. Category 2 or 3 events—gray or black water—typically require temporary relocation until remediation is complete and the space is cleared.

faqs.q: What happens if I wait to call after water damage?
faqs.a: Mold can begin colonizing within 24 to 48 hours in warm, moist conditions—common in Southern California interiors. Waiting converts a drying-only job into a full remediation project, raises costs significantly, and gives insurers grounds to reduce claim payments for preventable secondary damage.

faqs.q: What are common causes of water damage in a home?
faqs.a: Common causes include leaks from plumbing fixtures, burst pipes, roof leaks, flooding, appliance malfunctions, and sewer backups. In Southern California, we also see slab leaks in older Inland Empire homes, storm-driven roof intrusions, and irrigation-line failures against exterior walls.

faqs.q: How can I prevent water damage in my home?
faqs.a: Regularly inspect and maintain your plumbing, roof, and gutters. Install water leak detection systems, sump pumps, and backflow preventers where appropriate. Keep the home well-insulated and properly ventilated, and address minor drips before they become failures.

faqs.q: What long-term effects can water damage have on a home?
faqs.a: Untreated water damage can lead to mold growth, structural decay in framing and subfloor, compromised indoor air quality, corroded electrical components, and decreased property value. Professional remediation stops the damage progression and produces the documentation that keeps the loss out of future disclosure issues.
